content.value_statement: Astrale Domain development spans Schema, authorization, runtime, and deployment, which can become inconsistent. This skill guides focused changes and phased creation with explicit verification boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Guide project scaffolding, SDK imports, TypeScript configuration, and deployment environments.
Guide Schema authoring and distinguish callable authorization from graph access.
Explain Actions, Workflows, Queries, Mutations, and caller-scoped runtime authority.
Guide Integration and Provider boundaries, response validation, and secret isolation.
Guide browser Views, sample Datasets, and success and refusal testing.
Explain release installation, dependency upgrades, staged migrations, and live debugging.
limitations: This skill provides Markdown guidance, not a bundled SDK, CLI, or executable application.
Exact APIs depend on the installed SDK, CLI, adapter, and Domain source.
Live deployment and privileged operations require authorized identities, target instances, and suitable environment secrets.
The inline Workflow runner does not guarantee durable retries or exactly-once effects; migration authoring depends on available public APIs.

use_cases.title: Create a Business Domain
use_cases.description: Guide an application developer through project inspection, Schema design, callable implementation, sample data, and verification.

use_cases.title: Review Authorization Boundaries
use_cases.description: Help a security engineer examine callable admission, caller and principal authority, group membership, and refusal evidence.

use_cases.title: Qualify a Coordinated Release
use_cases.description: Help a release engineer plan coherent dependency upgrades, grouped installs, rollback constraints, and installed-behavior checks.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Existing Domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Astrale Domain project. Identify its Schema, runtime, environments, and verification commands. Explain missing prerequisites without deploying or changing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Protected Callable
prompt_templates.prompt: Add [operation] to [Class] using the installed SDK. Declare Schema-owned authorization and runtime behavior. Add allowed and refused tests without deploying.

prompt_templates.title: Implement an External Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [provider operation] through an Integration and Provider. Keep secrets environment-owned. Validate responses and test effects and failure behavior without claiming exactly-once delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dependency Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [Schema change] across affected Domains. Inspect installed revisions, design staged data migration, and specify grouped installs and rollback checks. Require approval before mutations.

output: Declare the callable input, output, authentication mode, and Policy in Schema.
Implement the admitted operation as a Workflow with named read and mutation steps.
Guard the state transition atomically rather than trusting the earlier read.
Test an allowed call, a Policy refusal, and a stale-state refusal.

output_examples.input: Plan an upgrade where employees depends on agencies.
output: Rebuild employees against the candidate agencies Schema revision.
Deploy both candidates and verify their served release metadata.
Install both as explicit roots in one grouped operation after approval.
Inspect installed revisions and retained behavior; preserve operation identity if the outcome is unknown.

output_examples.input: Diagnose a callable that works as Root but fails for a user.
output: Confirm the installed release, callable key, and registered caller identity.
Inspect the authenticated principal ceiling separately from caller Policy admission.
Verify the intended caller or self session and exact Domain requirements.
Repeat allowed and refused calls, then independently verify that refusal caused no effects.

best_practices: Inspect current source and installed public SDK exports before choosing API syntax.
Keep authorization in Schema, secrets in deployment environments, and tests focused on allowed and refused behavior.
Verify build, served release, installed revision, and live invocation separately before reporting deployment success.
anti_patterns: Do not weaken authentication or add handler authorization substitutes to make a failing test pass.
Do not put secrets in Schema, logs, test snapshots, source files, or command arguments.
Do not install coherent dependencies sequentially or treat deployment as installation.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides task-routed guidance for Astrale Domain authoring, authorization, runtime, Views, testing, migration, deployment, and debugging.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Project execution still depends on your installed Astrale tools and permissions.

faq.question: Does it include the Astrale SDK or CLI?
faq.answer: No. It contains Markdown instructions and references. Install compatible public SDK, CLI, and adapter packages for implementation and live verification.

faq.question: Does deployment update an instance?
faq.answer: No. Deployment creates a release endpoint. Installation separately changes the release pinned on the chosen instance.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Keep secrets in their owning deployment environment. Avoid source, logs, test evidence, and command arguments. Use private files or secret-manager input.

faq.question: Can it guarantee safe migrations or exactly-once delivery?
faq.answer: No. Migration support depends on public SDK contracts, and the inline Workflow runner does not provide durable replay or exactly-once execution.
